text.arabic_uthmani: فَلَوْلَا نَصَرَهُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ قُرْبَانًا ءَالِهَةًۢ ۖ بَلْ ضَلُّوا۟ عَنْهُمْ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْتَرُونَ

words.gloss_range: consequential resumptive particle opening a reproachful challenge
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) opens the ayah as a consequence marker. It resumes the preceding destruction scene (46:25-27) and turns that ruin into the premise for the failed-help question, so the interrogation begins as an inference from what has already been shown.

topics.headline: consequential challenge frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question is driven by the prior destruction rather than opening a new topic.
topics.reason: The particle is licensed as resumptive/consequential, and the discourse boundary rows tie it to the preceding destruction narrative.

topics.headline: prior ruin as premise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failed-help challenge functions like a prosecutorial conclusion from 46:25-27.
topics.reason: The boundary rows preserve the movement from displayed ruin to the present challenge.

words.gloss_range: reproachful interrogative particle, not the nominal counterfactual pattern
words.prose: {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) makes the opening question a rebuke: why did the expected rescue not occur? Its scope stretches through the long relative clause until the supposed helpers are finally named, so the first beat suspends the answer before the corrective particle overturns it.

topics.headline: reproach over counterfactual condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle asks a rebuking why-did-not question, not a neutral condition.
topics.reason: QAC and translation-support evidence identify the particle as reproachful interrogation before a perfect verb.

topics.headline: scope across first beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the challenge holds open until the whole adopted-god system has been named.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows coherently describe the particle scoping over the long relative clause and shifting the question into rebuke.

topics.headline: consequence plus challenge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary shift from evidence display into courtroom-like challenge.
topics.reason: The compound opening is supported by the preceding particle and by the ayah boundary profile.

words.gloss_range: completed active rescue/help tested against a visible object suffix
words.root_gloss_range: aid or support that would make someone prevail; unrelated branches such as rain, place-reaching, or affiliation are not active locally
words.prose: {{ar:نَصَرَهُمُ}} ({{tr:naṣarahumu}}) places the destroyed communities as the object of the rescue test before the supposed rescuers are named. The perfect verb makes the missing aid a completed failure, and the root field tests active intervention rather than symbolic closeness; the long-delayed subject then exposes adopted gods as unable to supply the rescue they were expected to provide. The false-helper challenge is a known test pattern (21:43; 36:74), while the repeated -hum thread carries the same participants from failed rescue to abandonment to verdict.

topics.headline: object suffix and completed failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the needy party before the helpers are identified, and hears the rescue failure as already settled.
topics.reason: QAC gives a perfect transitive verb with a third-person plural object suffix, matching the CRITICAL grammar rows.

topics.headline: active rescue field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question tests real intervention in crisis, while broader root branches are not locally selected.
topics.reason: V4 supports the aid/support branch for the local Form I verb, while unrelated root branches remain only background range.

topics.headline: delayed supposed helper
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the suspense created when the verb opens before its long subject complex.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following relative pronoun the subject and supports the delayed-subject reading.

topics.headline: recurring false-helper test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 46:28 specializes a recurring false-god help challenge (21:43; 36:74).
topics.reason: The concrete parallels name the same help-capacity test while the local access wording gives this ayah its special force.

topics.headline: repeated participant suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same participant thread moving from failed rescue to abandonment to verdict.
topics.reason: The suffix recurrence is a local phonetic and referential observation, not a separate lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: masculine plural relative pronoun serving as delayed subject head
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) begins the subject that should answer the rescue question. The pronoun grants the supposed helpers agent-like grammar long enough to test them, but the following clause defines them by human adoption, so the syntax turns claimed rescuers into products of the worshippers' own act.

topics.headline: relative subject delayed by clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rescuer identity is delayed and must be built by the following adoption clause.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the relative pronoun as subject of the rescue verb and head of the relative clause.

topics.headline: agent-like grammar exposes made objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that the idols receive agent-like grammar but are defined as humanly adopted objects.
topics.reason: The rational plural relative and the adoption clause coherently support the temporary agent-role reading.

topics.headline: syntactic delay mirrors constructed system
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the long relative clause postponing recognition of the failed helpers.
topics.reason: The structural rows describe the span from this relative head to the later deity noun.

words.gloss_range: completed deliberate adoption/taking for oneself, governing the false-god object and access role
words.root_gloss_range: taking, seizing, or adopting; local Form VIII selects deliberate self-involving adoption
words.prose: {{ar:ٱتَّخَذُوا۟}} ({{tr:ittakhadhū}}) is the engine of the relative clause. It presents the worshippers' adoption as a completed, chosen act and governs the later deity object together with the access-function word, so the expected helpers are introduced first as a constructed dependency. The recurring beside-God adoption formula appears here as an indictment pattern (25:3; 21:24; 46:28), and the compact doubled-t sound reinforces the constructed dependency rather than adding a new sense.

topics.headline: adoption frame with object and access role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb organizes both the deity object and the nearness role, while the exact accusative analysis remains open.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence strongly licenses the deity noun as object and the access noun as circumstantial or second-object pressure, so the topic is preserved with grammatical caution.

topics.headline: chosen self-involving adoption
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices culpable selection rather than accidental belief or bare possession.
topics.reason: QAC marks Form VIII and the CRITICAL form rows coherently read that as deliberate adoption.

topics.headline: settled human act before rescue test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human agency creates the supposed rescuers before they are tested.
topics.reason: The perfect verb and controlled plural subject support the completed human-act reading.

topics.headline: recurring beside-God adoption formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this is a local instance of a recurring indictment formula (25:3; 21:24; 46:28).
topics.reason: The cross-reference rows give concrete parallels, while local syntax specializes the formula through the access term.

topics.headline: relative-clause engine and compact sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how the verb drives the whole relative clause and audibly compresses the adoption form.
topics.reason: The structural and phonetic rows add local payoff without changing the lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: preposition fused with the following noun into a beside/apart-from exclusion frame
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) is not functioning as a loose source marker here. With the next word it forms the exclusion frame “besides/apart from God,” so distance from God is heard before the claim of nearness is introduced.

topics.headline: compound beside-God frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition helps create a fixed exclusion unit rather than a simple source phrase.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence treat the phrase with the following noun as a single governed construction.

topics.headline: separation before access claim

topics.reason: The local word order places the exclusion phrase before the access and deity nouns.

words.gloss_range: abstract noun in a governed beside/below-God exclusion phrase
words.root_gloss_range: below, besides, short of, and inferior relation; local phrase selects illegitimate substitution beside God
words.prose: {{ar:دُونِ}} ({{tr:dūni}}) turns spatial and hierarchical “below/beside” language into an exclusion relation. Governed by the preposition and bound to the divine name, it defines the adopted gods as substitutes measured against God, so the following nearness claim starts from a position of displacement and inferiority. The same beside-God dependence thread appears nearby in the surah (46:4; 46:5; 46:32), and the tight min-dun sound helps the exclusion phrase register as one unit.

topics.headline: governed construct relation to God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the relation is grammatically anchored to God, not free-floating otherness.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as governed by the preposition and heading the genitive relation to the divine name.

topics.headline: below and beside as failed substitution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that “beside” carries hierarchy and insufficiency, preparing the failed rescue.
topics.reason: V4 supports below/beside/short-of branches, and local syntax applies them to illegitimate substitutes.

topics.headline: fixed adverbial usage field

topics.reason: The contextual and CRITICAL distribution rows support the frozen nominal/adverbial function.

topics.headline: same-surah and cross-surah substitution echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same beside-God dependence thread appears nearby in the surah (46:4; 46:5; 46:32).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete same-surah and formulaic references, while local grammar controls their relevance.

topics.headline: axis before nearness claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exclusion phrase is heard before the claimed nearness device.
topics.reason: The structural and sound rows preserve local ordering and recitational cohesion.

words.gloss_range: definite proper divine name as genitive endpoint of the exclusion phrase
words.root_gloss_range: divinity/worship root family; local proper name is the singular divine reference point
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is the genitive endpoint that measures the whole beside/below relation. Its definite singular proper-name force stands before the later indefinite plural deity noun, making the contrast between the true reference point and manufactured substitutes grammatical as well as semantic. The same root family makes the true singular and false plural echo locally, while the proper-name status keeps them referentially distinct; this divine name also anchors the surah’s beside-God critique (46:4; 46:28; 46:32).

topics.headline: God as endpoint of exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exclusion relation is measured specifically against God.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the divine name the genitive complement of the beside/below noun.

topics.headline: proper singular against indefinite plural
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammatical contrast between the singular proper name and the later unspecified plural gods.
topics.reason: The local form contrast is explicit in QAC and in the CRITICAL morphology rows.

topics.headline: shared deity root contrast

topics.reason: The root relation is useful for contrast, but local grammar prevents treating the two nouns as the same referential category.

topics.headline: surah reference center

topics.reason: The same-surah rows provide concrete references and the local phrase supplies the contrast.

topics.headline: immediate contrast in word order and sound

topics.reason: The echo rows preserve proximity and contrast without changing the local syntax.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative access/offering noun, syntactically licensed as role, state, or purpose
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, approach, offering, and means of access; local rare noun selects devotional access/offering rather than generic closeness
words.prose: {{ar:قُرْبَانًا}} ({{tr:qurbānan}}) names the access mechanism before the deity noun arrives. Its accusative role is open between object, state, and purpose, but the surviving payoff is clear: the adopted gods are framed as a means of approach or offering, and that claimed nearness is later reversed into separation. The rare offering noun recalls concrete offering scenes (3:183; 5:27), while the paired indefinite cadence links the access-function and the gods as one constructed package.

topics.headline: accusative role with open parse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word is grammatically active in the adoption frame, while its exact accusative role remains contested.
topics.reason: Attachment supports a circumstantial role and QAC allows second-object pressure, so the topic is preserved with role ambiguity.

topics.headline: offering as means of nearness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the false worship system is portrayed as transactional access, not mere reverence.
topics.reason: V4 supports devotional approach and offering branches, and the local noun selects that concrete access function.

topics.headline: rare concrete access noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rare offering term against concrete offering scenes (3:183; 5:27).
topics.reason: The row family gives concrete recurrence references and the contextual profile marks the form as low occurrence.

topics.headline: sought nearness becomes distance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s core irony: the means chosen for nearness ends in going away.
topics.reason: The local sequence from this access noun to the disappearance verb licenses the reversal.

topics.headline: indefinite paired package
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paired indefinite cadence linking access-function and gods as one constructed package.

words.gloss_range: indefinite plural deity noun, object or apposition in the adoption frame
words.root_gloss_range: objects of worship or claimed deities; local syntax names humanly adopted gods, not proven divine reality
words.prose: {{ar:ءَالِهَةً}} ({{tr:ālihatan}}) is the delayed reveal of the first beat: the expected helpers are “gods,” but as an indefinite plural object of human adoption. The noun can be direct object or apposition to the access word; either way, the deity label is governed by a constructed access function and is immediately exposed by the failed rescue. The plural deity label also lands inside the recurring false-helper challenge (21:43; 36:74), with its marked onset and plural shape making the false label audibly distinct from the prior proper name.

topics.headline: object or appositive deity noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both parses make the gods part of a constructed adoption-and-access frame.
topics.reason: Attachment strongly licenses the noun as explicit object, while the CRITICAL rows preserve appositive pressure with the preceding access noun.

topics.headline: final reveal of failed helpers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the long first beat resolves only when the supposed helpers are named at the end.
topics.reason: The relative-subject chain and word order support the delayed reveal.

topics.headline: worship objects not divine proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the noun names what the worshippers made them into, not what the rescue test proves them to be.
topics.reason: The adoption verb and failed-help frame keep the deity noun under critique.

topics.headline: indefinite plural against proper singular
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the false pluralization against the earlier definite divine name.
topics.reason: The local root echo and form contrast are supported by adjacent wording.

topics.headline: recurring help challenge and marked ending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plural deity label lands inside a recognizable false-helper challenge (21:43; 36:74).
topics.reason: The intertext rows provide concrete parallels, and the phonetic row adds local closure detail.

words.gloss_range: corrective reversal particle cancelling the expected rescue proposition
words.prose: {{ar:بَلْ}} ({{tr:bal}}) is the ayah’s hinge. After the long challenge asks why help did not come, this short particle cancels the expected rescue and introduces the opposite: the supposed helpers vanished away instead.

topics.headline: corrective cancellation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle overturns the expected rescue rather than merely adding a next event.
topics.reason: QAC identifies corrective force, and the following disappearance clause supplies the replacement.

topics.headline: answer to the opening challenge

topics.reason: The structural rows coherently connect the opening reproach and the middle reversal.

topics.headline: clipped rhythmic break
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sudden compressed break after the long first beat.
topics.reason: The particle’s standalone form and phonetic row support the audible hinge payoff.

words.gloss_range: completed plural intransitive straying/disappearing away from the worshippers
words.root_gloss_range: going astray, being lost, disappearing, or failing to be found; local Form I with a following separation phrase selects vanished/strayed-away failure
words.prose: {{ar:ضَلُّوا۟}} ({{tr:ḍallū}}) supplies the substance of the reversal. The supposed helpers do not merely fail to answer; in the selected Form I and with the following separation phrase, they are portrayed as having gone astray or vanished away from the worshippers, turning the promised nearness into distance. This false-object loss motif recurs in verdict scenes (7:53; 10:30), and here it lands as the first content word after the corrective pivot.

topics.headline: completed straying away
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reversal is a completed loss directed away from the very people expecting aid.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect plural verb, and attachment identifies the following prepositional complement.

topics.headline: astray and disappeared range localized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both error and disappearance pressure, while local grammar favors intransitive vanished-away failure over causative misguidance.
topics.reason: V4 supports astray/disappearance branches, and QAC/attachment favor Form I intransitive behavior with a separation complement.

topics.headline: nearness reversed into distance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the core antithesis between sought approach and actual departure.
topics.reason: The access noun earlier in the ayah and this disappearance verb form a coherent local reversal.

topics.headline: false objects lost to users
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recurring Quranic motif of false objects being lost from their users (7:53; 10:30).
topics.reason: The concrete parallels preserve recurrence without governing the local parse.

topics.headline: first content word after reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices disappearance landing immediately after the corrective particle.
topics.reason: The structural and phonetic rows add local force to the reversal.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus plural suffix marking separation away from the abandoned worshippers
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) completes the reversal as relational abandonment. It prevents the verb from closing as generic straying and makes the direction “away from them,” returning the hearer to the same people whose rescue had been questioned.

topics.headline: separation away from them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the loss is directed away from the worshippers, not merely stated absolutely.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence governs the suffix by the preposition with the preceding verb.

topics.headline: same group from rescue to abandonment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the group needing rescue is the same group abandoned by the supposed helpers.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence and the suffix echo support participant continuity.

topics.headline: reversal closes on abandoned party
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the middle beat ending on the abandoned people.
topics.reason: The structural and sound rows preserve the local endpoint of the reversal.

words.gloss_range: coordinating/resumptive connector introducing the verdict clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does not let the ayah stop at disappearance. It links the failed-help event to a formal evaluation, so the demonstrative verdict arrives as a direct assessment of the whole scene. The connector can be heard as coordination with the reversal and as resumption into a fresh evaluative beat.

topics.headline: event linked to verdict

topics.reason: QAC marks coordination and the attachment profile identifies the following nominal verdict clause.

topics.headline: coordination and resumption together

topics.reason: The exact clause hierarchy can be read two ways, but both preserve the local connection between event and verdict.

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative gathering the preceding scene as subject of a nominal verdict
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) gathers the adoption, failed rescue, and disappearance into one pointed object of judgment. As the subject of a nominal sentence, it turns the event sequence into a stable verdict: that whole system is what the next word names.

topics.headline: demonstrative gathers the whole scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demonstrative points to the entire preceding scenario, not one nearby noun.
topics.reason: Attachment cross-reference evidence says the demonstrative points to the failed divine-association claim just described.

topics.headline: scene held apart for judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the scene being set at evaluative distance before it is named.
topics.reason: The distal demonstrative and verdict position support this evaluative pointing.

topics.headline: standing nominal verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the opening challenge closing as a judgment rather than another narrative event.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a nominal sentence with the following predicate.

words.gloss_range: construct verdict noun with suffix: their inversion/falsehood as predicate of the demonstrative
words.root_gloss_range: turning away, inversion, falsehood, and overturning; local gerund names the failed system as their owned or consequential inversion
words.prose: {{ar:إِفْكُهُمْ}} ({{tr:ifkuhum}}) is the first verdict label. As predicate of the demonstrative, it names the whole failed system as their inversion or falsehood, and the suffix keeps that diagnosis attached to them. The construct can hold both their production of falsehood and the falsehood that overtook them, while variant readings expose result, action, and agent without displacing the local noun parse. The overturning root image recalls the overturned-city field (53:53; 69:9), and the same-surah movement turns an earlier charge of turning away into a closing verdict (46:22; 46:28).

topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the predicate of the demonstrative, and morphology supplies the construct suffix.

topics.headline: agency and consequence in construct

topics.reason: The construct relation supports subjective and objective genitive pressure without requiring a single English expansion.

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) controls the final clause’s relation to the verdict. words.gloss_range: perfect auxiliary with plural subject, making the final verb past habitual/continuous
words.root_gloss_range: being, occurrence, or temporal predication; local auxiliary marks a past sustained predicate rather than independent existence
words.prose: {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) stretches the final accusation backward as an ongoing habit. It is an auxiliary governing the following imperfect verb, so fabrication is not one isolated claim but the past condition repeatedly defining the same people. The plural ending keeps the fabricators present without renaming them, and the auxiliary-plus-imperfect shape carries the long-vowel cadence into the final verdict word.

topics.headline: past habitual auxiliary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final falsehood is portrayed as an ongoing past practice, not a one-time act.

words.gloss_range: imperfect Form VIII fabrication verb governed by the auxiliary, with object supplied by the preceding particle
words.root_gloss_range: local grammar selects forged fabrication; V4 branches for the normalized root do not support importing a divine-origination contrast
words.prose: {{ar:يَفْتَرُونَ}} ({{tr:yaftarūn}}) is the ayah’s final action word: the same people were habitually fabricating. Its object is compactly supplied by the preceding particle and verdict noun, so the ending does not restate the false content; it closes by naming ongoing counterfeit production. The Form VIII and plural imperfect ending keep collective forged agency audible at closure, and the final verb joins recurring falsehood codas (6:24; 6:138; 7:53; 10:30; 11:21). Root-level claims that contrast this word with divine origination are blocked by the supplied V4 root data, but the local fabrication sense and formulaic closure remain intact.

topics.headline: object supplied and habitual aspect
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verb has a compact object and is made habitual by the preceding auxiliary.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the preceding particle as object and the auxiliary as governing this predicate action.

topics.headline: deliberate fabrication not neutral making

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The rhetorical demand for aid, the deliberate taking of a qurban as gods other than God, and the helpers' disappearance.
baseline_models.mechanism: Agents acquire objects of worship as means of approach and thereby load the relation with an expectation of aid. When the supposed helpers cannot be found at the test, their absence exposes both the mediating arrangement and its claimed efficacy as fabricated.

activation_trace.role: Aid and making one prevail supply the performance expected from the adopted mediators and tested by the opening question.
Making or acquiring something for oneself marks the gods as deliberately installed relational assets rather than accidental errors.
Otherness and lower rank locate the acquired gods outside and beneath the divine endpoint they were meant to mediate.
Being made an object of worship identifies both the true divine pole and the manufactured divine substitutes in the relation.
An offering or means used to seek approach supplies the mediating function for which the adopted gods were valued.
Loss and inability to locate a thing turn failed help into the concrete nonavailability of the alleged helpers.
A lie diverted from truth names the false claim that this installed relation could secure approach and aid.
Inventing falsehood makes the failed mediation an authored construction repeatedly maintained by its adherents.

changed_reading.before: A general rebuke that false gods did not help their worshippers.
changed_reading.after: A failed nearness contract: worshippers deliberately installed mediating gods to secure approach and expected aid, but nonappearance under test discloses the whole relation as their own fabrication.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The qurban-as-gods construction beside the demand that those adopted figures render aid.
baseline_models.mechanism: The nearness term can evoke a ruler's intimates and courtiers as well as an offering. On this reading the adopted gods are imagined as insiders close enough to convey access and patronage; their disappearance strips them of the courtly presence on which that claim depends.

activation_trace.role: Favored intimates and a ruler's inner circle supply the social model of divine access assigned to the adopted gods.
Nearness that remains short of the goal positions the alleged courtiers as intermediate rather than ultimate.
Deliberate acquisition makes patron status something the worshippers confer and maintain.
Support and prevailing define the patronage service expected from figures claimed to be near the sovereign.
Vanishing from view removes the supposed insiders precisely when their presence should matter.

changed_reading.before: Qurban names only sacrificial offerings made to separate gods.
changed_reading.after: The construction can also stage those gods as self-appointed divine courtiers: claimed insiders expected to patronize their clients, yet absent when their access is tested.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence of taking, seeking nearness, going astray or missing, inversion, and fabrication.
baseline_models.mechanism: The closing pair need not be redundant labels for lying. Inversion supplies a directional operation that turns attachment from its proper end, while fabrication supplies the making of the mediating device; the vanished gods reveal a constructed system of diversion.

activation_trace.role: Making something one's own begins the human construction of the substitute relation.
A means intended to bring one near supplies the advertised direction of the constructed device.
Deviation from the intended course registers the device's actual directional result.
Turning a thing away from its proper face supplies the reversal by which alleged approach becomes diversion.
Cutting and joining material to fashion something supplies a controlled making analogy for the manufactured religious system.

changed_reading.before: The final two expressions simply repeat that the worshippers lied.
changed_reading.after: The ending exposes a made diversion: they fashioned a means advertised as approach, but its operation reversed direction and left both adherents and helpers lost.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier sequence turns the focus question into a diagnosis of a nonreciprocal relationship. The worshippers call, receive no answer, and address beings unaware of the call; at gathering, the same beings become enemies and repudiate the worship. Failure to help is therefore not one missed intervention but the exposure and reversal of an empty channel.

activation_trace.role: Expected aid is the focus-side service whose relational preconditions the earlier sequence tests.
Seeking approach supplies the intended bond that the call-and-answer sequence shows to be nonreciprocal.
Calling and drawing another by speech establishes the attempted communication channel to the other-than-God addressees.
Returning speech or answering supplies the reciprocal act explicitly absent from that channel.
Inattention that leaves something outside awareness explains why the call never becomes a mutual relation.
Enmity turns passive nonresponse into an active reversal of the patron-client expectation.
Submissive worship names the human investment that receives neither recognition nor aid and is finally repudiated.

structural_cues: 46:4-6 moves from inspecting invoked beings, through nonresponse and unawareness, to gathered hostility and repudiation.
The repeated worshipper-addressee relation is the same relation whose capacity for aid is tested in 46:28.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies invocation, absent answer, unawareness, worship, and eventual enmity; I infer that usable aid presupposes recognition and reciprocity, so the sequence diagnoses the channel itself as empty. A live alternative is that 46:6 marks only a future reversal rather than present relational nullity.

changed_reading.before: The adopted gods happen to fail during one crisis.
changed_reading.after: Their failed aid reveals a channel that was never reciprocal: call meets no answer or awareness, and the supposed bond ultimately reverses into enmity and repudiation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the earlier context, fabrication and inversion are accusations directed at the message, while the warning is charged with turning people away from their gods. The focus demonstrative returns those same operations to the worshippers: the allegedly diverting message is not the fabrication; their divinized mediation is the manufactured diversion.

activation_trace.role: Directional inversion in the focus supplies the operation whose ownership is reassigned by the contextual accusations.
Invented falsehood in the focus identifies the worshippers' system as the actual object of the repeated fabrication charge.
The repeated accusation of invented falsehood supplies the contested label that the focus later redirects.
Calling the received message an old lie establishes the worshippers' prior assignment of the falsehood label.
The charge of being turned away supplies the precise directional accusation reversed by the focus.
The worshipped gods identify what the speakers fear losing when they portray warning as diversion.

structural_cues: 46:8, 46:11, and 46:22 repeatedly place fabrication or diversion language inside contested speech before 46:28's demonstrative judgment.
The immediate destruction narrative intervenes before the focus returns the charge to the failed divine substitutes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated accusation vocabulary and a later demonstrative judgment; I infer a deliberate polemical return of the labels from revelation to the manufactured cult. The recurrence could instead be non-directional thematic repetition, leaving the focus as a simple independent verdict.

changed_reading.before: The ending independently labels idolatry as lie and fabrication.
changed_reading.after: The ending adjudicates a struggle over labels: those who called revelation fabricated and diverting are shown to have fabricated the very diversion they defended.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding cloud scene activates the rain-and-relief branch of aid. A cloud is read as incoming rain, but the adversative reversal identifies a punitive wind; it destroys, endowed faculties do not suffice, and signs are turned through different presentations. The focus question then repeats that perceptual failure socially: a form expected to deliver relief proves to be an inverted carrier of ruin, just as adopted patrons expected to help disappear.

activation_trace.role: Rain as rescue and life-giving aid opens the focus verb to the material expectation staged by the approaching cloud.
Winds that shift from their expected courses provide a weather-shaped image for the focus's inversion.
Water descending from cloud supplies the community's expected rescue reading of the visible form.
Rain associated with punishment keeps the same material sign while reversing its expected benefit.
Blowing wind supplies the actual carrier concealed beneath the mistaken rain-cloud interpretation.
Painful punishment supplies the destructive payload that replaces expected relief.
Extirpating destruction makes the consequence of the mistaken rescue reading materially complete.
Sufficiency and availing establish the negative utility test that immediately anticipates the focus's failed help.
Turning something through different states supplies the final transition from varied signs to the focus's exposed inversion.

structural_cues: 46:24 explicitly reverses the inhabitants' rain interpretation before 46:25-27 narrates destruction, non-availing capacities, and varied signs.
46:28 follows without a scene break and asks why the adopted divine means did not provide aid.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a cloud called rain, an explicit reversal to punitive wind, destruction, non-availing faculties, and the focus root's rain-rescue branch; I infer that adjacency carries this material rescue failure into the patronage question. The live alternative is that the focus verb retains only ordinary social or military help with no weather echo.

changed_reading.before: The false gods simply fail to intervene after a destroyed people call on them.
changed_reading.after: Their failure repeats the cloud's inverted promise: what was read as a vehicle of rescue carried ruin, so apparent nearness and apparent relief are exposed by the same misrecognition.

context_deltas.mechanism: After the focus, a group is turned toward the recitation, hears with understanding, comes into presence, listens silently, and then urges its people to answer God's caller. Answering yields protective adjacency, while refusal leaves no escape and no supporting patrons besides Him. This supplies a counter-model of approach: nearness is enacted by receptive response, not manufactured by acquiring divine intermediaries.

activation_trace.role: Claimed intimate access supplies the false patronage model that the following responsive sequence replaces.
Aid is the failed outcome against which genuine answering and protection are measured.
Being turned toward a new face begins a successful redirection rather than the focus's deceptive diversion.
Hearing as understanding and compliance makes reception functionally responsive rather than merely acoustic.
Presence, witnessing, and nearness supply an enacted approach that contrasts with claimed cultic proximity.
Attentive silence supplies the receptive posture through which the new relation becomes effective.
Returning the call supplies the reciprocal act missing from the false-god relationship.
The voiced summons identifies the legitimate call whose answer establishes relation.
Neighboring protection supplies the real shelter promised through response, countering merely alleged patronage.
Failure to outrun or escape closes the possibility that another route can compensate for refusing the call.
Otherness marks the same alternative divine space occupied by the failed intermediaries in the focus.
Loving alliance and support name the patronage explicitly unavailable outside the legitimate relation.
Deviation from the right course names the condition produced by refusing the responsive path.

structural_cues: 46:29-31 forms a response chain: redirection, hearing, presence, attentive silence, return to a people, and an appeal to answer.
46:32 closes the chain with no escape and no patrons other than God, directly echoing the focus's other-than-God helpers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the response chain, protective adjacency, and explicit denial of other patrons; I infer that it is a positive counter-model to the focus's purchased nearness. A live alternative is that the post-focus episode illustrates warning and accountability without defining the earlier qurban relation.

changed_reading.before: The ayah only negates access through false intermediaries.
changed_reading.after: The following sequence also discloses an alternative approach: turn, attend, understand, and answer the legitimate call; protective nearness follows response, while manufactured patrons provide neither answer nor aid.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates peripheral water-channel, reservoir, water-seeking, and rain-deprivation branches across several focus roots. It remains anchored in the focus's aid, taking, approach, and inversion lexemes and is materially activated by the adjacent cloud scene. Downstream prose should present it only as a hydrological analogy for failed mediation, never as the direct lexical translation of the ayah.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The cluster of aid, deliberate taking, qurban-nearness, and inversion immediately after a cloud expected to bring rain.

activation_trace.role: Watercourses arriving from afar into a collection point supply a channel model for expected aid.
A hollow that captures and retains water supplies the receiving infrastructure assigned to the adopted means.
Moving toward a water source supplies the promised motion from need toward relief.
Land deprived of rain supplies the failed endpoint of a channel that promised water but delivered none.
Rainwater from the cloud provides the adjacent material expectation that activates the focus cluster.
Wind replacing expected rain supplies the misrouting event that defeats the imagined delivery system.

changed_reading.before: The false gods fail only as personal helpers.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, the cult resembles a misrouted water-delivery system: channels, capture, and approach promise relief, but the arriving wind leaves the expected recipients without rain or aid.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it uses the packet's non-dominant mapped inventory for the final focus root, activating slackening after intensity rather than the ordinary fabrication sense. It remains valid as a secondary echo anchored in that exact focus occurrence and the failed-help sequence. Downstream prose must qualify it as an associative activation and must not replace the ordinary meaning of fabrication with faltering.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The final focus verb's split root mapping, following the helpers' failure and disappearance.

activation_trace.role: Weakening and subsiding after sharpness supply an echo in which the alleged patrons' manufactured potency slackens at the decisive test.
The demand for effective aid provides the test against which that exploratory slackening becomes visible.
Disappearance supplies the observable collapse that permits the faltering echo without changing the base lexical reading.
The prior failure of endowed capacities to avail supplies a nearby pattern of apparent power becoming functionally inert.

changed_reading.before: The closing verb only states that the worshippers kept inventing claims.
changed_reading.after: Without displacing that meaning, the split inventory permits an exploratory echo: the potency they fabricated for their patrons slackens into inactivity exactly when aid is demanded.

strongest_changes: The nonresponse sequence changes one failed rescue into exposure of a relation that never possessed recognition or reciprocity and ultimately reverses into enmity.
The adjacent cloud scene activates aid as rain-relief, making the focus repeat a concrete reversal in which an apparent vehicle of rescue carries destruction.
The post-focus answer chain supplies a positive counter-model: receptive hearing and response create protective nearness, while acquired patrons offer neither answer nor aid.
Repeated accusations of fabrication and diversion are returned to the worshippers, so the ending resolves a contested attribution rather than merely adding generic blame.
summary.what_was_special: The focus supports several coexisting mechanisms: ritual mediation, courtier-style patronage, a constructed directional diversion, a rain-rescue reversal, and a contrast between purchased proximity and responsive proximity. Peripheral hydrological branches and the non-dominant split mapping preserve activations that a conservative synthesis would likely erase.
remaining_uncertainties: The qurban construction can sustain offering, means-of-approach, and courtier-intimacy readings without forcing one syntactic resolution.
The rain-rescue model depends on immediate context activating a peripheral aid branch; ordinary social help remains fully live.
The post-focus response chain may be a deliberate counter-model of nearness or a separate illustration of warning and accountability.
The faltering sense from the non-dominant final-root mapping is associative and should never displace the primary fabrication reading.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A device of approach fails at the moment aid is needed.** ق ر ب B005 is devotional approach and offering; ن ص ر B001 is aid that makes someone prevail. The adopted gods are grammatically made a `قربانا`, an access mechanism, yet they provide no aid. I infer that claimed access is being tested by operational rescue. The ayah reads as failure of a mediation system, not only absence of divine helpers.
2. **The mediators disappear from the relation they were meant to close.** ض ل ل B002 is being hidden or disappearing and B003 is failing to locate something. This realizes the latent disappearance in 46:5. I infer that the attempted nearness of `قربانا` collapses into unlocatability. The sharper irony is spatial: what was adopted to reduce distance becomes absent.
3. **Diversion and fabrication name different failures.** ء ف ك B001 is turning from proper direction and B002 is a lie diverted from truth; ف ر ي B003 is fabricating a lie. The first assigns the false system a directional effect, while the second assigns its makers a constructive act. I infer a two-stage mechanism: they manufacture the claim, and the claim turns practice off course. These readings should remain distinct.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 46:29–31 immediately replace vanished mediators with listeners who become real warners and call toward an answerable relation. The contrast confirms that effective nearness is measured by response and protection, not cultic designation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Adopted means of approach prove structurally short of the source they were meant to access.** `ٱتَّخَذُوا` activates ء خ ذ B010, adopting or taking something for oneself; `مِن دُونِ` activates د و ن B003, besides, with B001 retaining the image of what is near yet lower or short of something, and `قُرْبَانًا` activates ق ر ب B005, a devotional offering or means of approach. The packet says that these objects were adopted as gods and as approach-means apart from God. I infer a failed access architecture: the worshippers assign mediating nearness to entities whose stated relation remains below and apart from the source. The claimed bridge encodes its own insufficiency.

2. **The support test ends not merely in weakness but in the disappearance of the supposed supporters.** `نَصَرَهُم` activates ن ص ر B001, aid that makes another prevail; `ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ` activates ض ل ل B002, becoming hidden or disappearing, together with B003, being lost and unfindable. The reproach `فَلَوْلَا` asks why the adopted gods did not help, and `بَلْ` replaces that expected aid with their absence. The packet gives failed support and disappearance; I infer that crisis exposes a category error in the relationship: what was treated as an available patron cannot even be located in the decisive relation. Their absence is the empirical collapse of the adopted system.

3. **Fabrication is a cut-and-joined directional construction that cannot survive its own test.** `إِفْكُهُمْ` activates ء ف ك B001, turning something from its direction, and B002, the resulting lie; `يَفْتَرُونَ` activates ف ر ي B001, cutting material in order to fit or stitch it, and B003, fabricating a lie. The packet itself identifies the vanished mediation as their `إفك` and fabrication. I infer that the false system is not random error but assembled misdirection: separate claims were cut and joined into an apparent route of access. When no help arrives, both the direction and the joins are exposed as invented.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 46:31–32 replaced fabricated mediation with a direct call-and-answer structure: response through ج و ب B003 brings sanctuary through ج و ر B003, while nonresponse has no alternative allies through و ل ي B004. These later ayat sharpened 46:28’s vanished gods as an unnecessary as well as ineffective access system.

baseline.text: Allah'ın dışında, O'na yaklaştırıcı tanrılar edindikleri şeyler onlara yardım etseydi ya! Aksine, onlar kendilerinden kaybolup gittiler. Bu, onların yalanı ve uydurdukları şeydir.

findings.text: Yaklaştırıcı diye benimsenen ilahlar, ihtiyaç anında üstünlük sağlayan yardım üretemeyince aracılık düzeni işlevsel bir kurtarma sınavında çöker.
Allah'tan ayrı ve O'ndan aşağıda kalan varlıkları yaklaşma köprüsü yapmak, erişim düzeninin içine daha baştan kaynağa ulaşamama eksikliğini yerleştirir.
Mesafeyi azaltmak için seçilen aracılar belirleyici anda bulunamaz hâle gelerek yakınlık iddiasını ilişkisel yokluğa çevirir.
Uydurma ile saptırma iki ayrı aşama oluşturur: iddia parçalar birleştirilerek imal edilir, sonra bu imal edilmiş düzen davranışı doğru yönünden çevirir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P3 (46:26-35): Proximity and Protection Put to Test
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Claimed nearness is valid only if it can answer, assist, cover fault, and secure escape under pressure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Offering, neighborhood asylum, pursuit, and covering branches translate religious relation into enforceable protection.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Manufactured proximity cannot produce help
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Objects are adopted and offered as means of nearness, but disappear precisely when assistance is required.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: Acquiring or adopting (`quranic:root_000018:B010/m01`); an offering that establishes proximity (`quranic:root_001212:B005/m01`); an object of worship (`quranic:root_000047:B001/m01`); assistance (`quranic:root_001510:B001/m01`); something lost or vanished (`quranic:root_000913:B003/m01`); fabricated falsehood (`quranic:root_001150:B003/m01`).

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Sacral proximity is judged by performance under need; disappearance at the point of aid exposes both the adopted objects and the fabrication that sustained them.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiye ya da topluluğa yardım ederek onu güçlendirmek ve özellikle bir düşman karşısında üstün duruma gelmesini sağlamaktır; karşılıklı biçiminde taraflar birbirine yardım eder.

Karşılıklı kullanımda birden çok tarafın birbirine yardım etmesi ve iş birliği yapması anlatılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hem yağmurun adı ve tam bir yağış oluşunu hem de yağmurun toprağı sulaması, yeşertmesi ve insanları sıkıntıdan kurtarmasını birlikte bildirir. Verilen dal çerçevesi yağış ile onun yararlı sonucunu doğru bir bütünlük içinde tutar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, suyun aktığı yatağı değil, yağan yağmuru ve onun toprakla insanlar üzerindeki yararlı etkisini anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yağmur adını ve tam yağış biçimini; toprağın yağmur alması, yağmurun sulayıp yeşertmesi ve insanların yağmurla ferahlaması yapılarından ayrı gösterir.

concept_map.definition: Yağmurun kendisini, özellikle yeterli ve yararlı bir yağışı adlandırır. İlgili yapılarda yağmurun toprağı sulayıp yeşertmesi, toprağın yağmur alması ve insanların yağmurla sıkıntıdan kurtulması anlatılır.

facets.statement: Yağmurun adı ve özellikle eksiksiz, yeterli bir yağış oluşu bu dalın adlandırma çekirdeğidir.
Yağmurun ülkeyi veya toprağı sulaması ve bitki çıkarması, yararlı etkinin başlıca gerçekleşmesidir.
Toprağın yağmur almış duruma gelmesi, olayın etkilenen yer açısından kurulan biçimidir.
Bir topluluğun yağmura kavuşarak kuraklık veya susuzluktan kurtulması, etkinin insanlar açısından kurulan biçimidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yağmur adını, yeterli yağışı, toprağın yağmur almasını ve yağmurun sulama, yeşertme ve insanları rahatlatma sonuçlarını aynı anlam alanında birleştirir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi doğrudan verme ve armağan anlamını, daha genel biçimde de iyi bir şeyi ulaştırma veya sunma düşüncesini bildirir. Verilen çerçeve bu iki yönü yardım ve yağmur dallarına taşırmadan doğru biçimde birleştirir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, birine destek olmanın her türünü değil, iyi bir şeyi ona verme veya ulaştırma eylemini anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, çıplak dalın armağan ve iyilik verme kapsamını korur; yağmur veya belirli bir yardım yapısı bu anlama eklenmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi Hristiyanlığı, bu dine girme ve birini bu dine sokma eylemlerini, bağlı kişi ile topluluğun adlarını ve adlandırmanın kökenine dair iki açıklamayı birlikte verir. Dal çerçevesi temel din ve bağlılık alanını doğru kurar; köken açıklamaları anlamın kendisi değildir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Adın yardımcılar düşüncesiyle ilişkilendirilmesi, bu dalı yardım anlamına dönüştürmez; din ve bağlılık çekirdeği korunur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, Hristiyanlık alanındaki din, bağlılık, dine girme ve dine sokma biçimlerini kapsar; adın kökenine ilişkin açıklamalar yalnızca ikincil bilgi olarak tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Hristiyanlığı, bu dine bağlı olmayı, bu dine girmeyi veya birini bu dine sokmayı ve bağlı kişi ya da topluluğu adlandıran anlam alanıdır. Adın kökeni için Tanrı'nın yardımcıları olma çağrısına ve bir yer adına bağlanan iki açıklama aktarılır; bunlar temel anlamı belirlemez.

facets.statement: Hristiyanlık ve bu dine bağlılık, dalın din ve kimlik çekirdeğini oluşturur.
Bir kişinin Hristiyanlığı benimseyip bu dine girmesi, bağlılığın oluşma sürecidir.
Bir başkasını Hristiyan yapmak, sürecin dışarıdan bir etkileyenle kurulan ettirgen biçimidir.
Dine bağlı erkek, kadın ve topluluk için kullanılan adlar aynı kimlik alanını kişi ve grup düzeyinde kurar.
Adlandırmanın kökeni bir açıklamada Tanrı'nın yardımcıları olma çağrısına, diğerinde bir yer adına bağlanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlam alanı Hristiyanlık, bu dine girme veya sokma ve bağlı kişileri adlandırmadır. Adın kökeni için Tanrı'nın yardımcıları düşüncesine ve bir yer adına dayanan iki farklı açıklama aktarılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, uzaktaki bir yerden gelip vadiye veya suyun toplandığı yere ulaşan yarıntı ve su yataklarını açıkça tanımlar. Dal çerçevesi bu yer biçimini yağmurun kendisinden ve genel su akışından doğru biçimde ayırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Uzak bir başlangıçtan su toplanma yerine uzanan yatak veya yarıntı belirleyicidir; yalnız suyun akması yeterli değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım kanıtlanan çoğul su yatağı adını esas alır ve incelemede tutulan iki olası tekil biçimi yalnız kendi sözlüksel satırlarında gösterir; çıplak köke genel su yolu anlamı verilmez.

concept_map.definition: Uzak bir yerden başlayıp vadiye veya suyun biriktiği yere ulaşan doğal yarıntı, dere kolu ya da su yatağıdır.

facets.statement: Su yatağı veya yarıntı uzaktaki bir yerden gelir ve vadiye ya da su toplanma yerine ulaşır.
Adlandırma, suyun aktığı yatak ile bu yatağı oluşturan doğal yarıntı görünümünü birlikte kapsayabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Dal, uzaktan gelen suyu vadiye veya su toplanma yerine taşıyan doğal yatak ve yarıntıların sınırlı adlandırmasını temsil eder.

source_details.summary: Bu kullanım yalnız bir kaynakta, uzaktan gelip vadideki su toplanma yerine ulaşan yarıntı ve su yolları olarak tanıklanır.

concept_gloss.text: uzaktan gelip su toplanma yerine ulaşan su yatağı

error_profile.preserves: Uzak başlangıcı, su taşıyan doğal yolu ve vadi ya da toplanma yerindeki son noktayı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Doğal yarıntının ana vadiye uzaktan katılan bir dere kolu olarak görüldüğü coğrafi bağlamlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Uzak başlangıçtan ana su alanına uzanan doğal kol görünümünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Her kullanımda açık bir dere bulunmayabileceğini ve hedefin genel bir su toplanma yeri olabileceğini daraltır.

error_profile.preserves: Suyu taşıyan yolu ve yolun su toplanma yerine bağlanmasını korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yatak uzaktaki kaynaktan vadiye veya suyun toplandığı yere doğru gelir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal yolu başlangıç ve varış ilişkisiyle tanımlar; komşu dal ise vadinin veya tepenin aşağı ucu ve kuyruk biçimine odaklanır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Doğal yarıntının uzaktan gelip su birikim alanına ulaşması belirleyicidir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal doğal ve uzak kaynaklı yataktır; komşu dal suyu yönlendiren kanal ile akışı açma veya engelleme işlemlerini de kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Belirli uzak başlangıç ile vadi veya toplanma yeri arasındaki yatak adlandırılır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Suyun veya başka bir şeyin akma olayı, akıtılması ve akan suyun kendisi merkezdedir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Su, doğal yatağı içinde ilerlerken yer biçimi ile akış olayı aynı sahnede buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal suyun izlediği belirli arazi biçimidir; komşu dal ise akma olayını, akan suyu ve akıtma eylemini daha genel biçimde anlatır.

root_profile.summary: Kök; yardım edip üstünlük sağlama ve haksızlığa karşı hakkını alma alanlarının yanında bir yere gelme, yağmurla sulama ve rahatlatma, iyilik verme, Hristiyanlık aidiyeti ve uzaktan gelen su yatakları gibi belirgin biçimde ayrılan anlam dalları kurar. Bazı dallar yardım ve yarar düşüncesiyle ilişkilendirilebilse de din adı, yer yönelimi ve su yatağı gibi kollar bağımsız sınırlar taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi edinme alanına almayı, ona erişip onu toplamayı ve ele geçirmeyi ortak çekirdek olarak verir. Dalın genel çerçevesi bu çekirdeği doğru yansıtır; bu çekirdekten türeyen emir ve kalıplaşmış kullanımlar ise ayrı sözlüksel birimler olarak tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği genel edinme ve ele alma eylemidir; tutsak etme, suçtan sorumlu tutma ve öteki özel kullanımlar buna katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım genel eylem çekirdeğini verir; emir biçimi ile söz, yular ve nesne çevresindeki kalıplı kullanımların kapsamı ayrıca korunur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi erişim ve denetim alanına getirerek ele geçirmek, edinmek ya da bir araya toplamaktır.

facets.statement: Bir nesneye erişme, onu ele geçirme ve kendi denetim alanına alma eylemini anlatır.
Ele geçirilen şeylerin toplanıp bir araya getirilmesi de aynı genel eylem çekirdeğinin kapsamındadır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, erişip alma ile denetim altına alma ve toplama yönlerini aynı temel eylemin bileşenleri olarak birleştirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir şeyin erişim ve denetim alanına alınmasını, gerektiğinde toplanmasını birlikte anlatan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Erişme, ele geçirme, edinme ve toplama çekirdeğini birlikte korur.

error_profile.loses: Denetim altına alma ve bir araya toplama yönlerini açıkça söylemez.
